Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

discuss verb

also discussion, talk over, talk it over, discuss in person, face to face, discuss face to face, one on one, discuss privately

classical

Cic. Att. 4.4.1: cētera cōram agēmus
Cic. Att. 3.9.2: sed tēcum haec omnia cōram agēmus
Traupman 97: cōram id agere possumus, we can discuss that face to face
Traupman 105: we can discuss that one on one, id cōram agere possumus
Traupman 312

agō, agere, ēgī, āctum

verb, third conjugation; dē and the ablative for the subject, cum and the ablative for the person · Conjugation on Wiktionary

discuss, talk over (with someone)

Lewis & Short: agere cum aliquō dē aliquā rē, “to treat, deal, negotiate, confer, talk with one about a person or thing”. Cicero ends letters with cētera cōram, “the rest when we meet”.

Other words

  • disputō, disputāre, disputāvī, disputātum — discuss, argue out (a question)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 26, 29: Disputābimus dē illā rē crās; Cic. Rep. 1.10 (Lewis & Short): dē mōribus, dē virtūtibus, dē rē pūblicā; Traupman 304 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    With dē and the ablative; Lewis & Short: to discuss a doubtful subject, “very freq. in Cicero’s philos. and rhet. writings”. Traupman’s word for “discuss”.

  • disserō, disserere, disseruī, dissertum — discuss, talk at length about

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Lael. 33: quae saepissimē inter mē et Scīpiōnem dē amīcitiā disserēbantur · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Of setting out a subject in a long talk.

  • disputātiō, disputātiōnis f. — a discussion

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 29; Cic. Off. 1.7: omnis disputātiō dē officiō futūra est; Traupman 304 · Declension on Wiktionary

    For a chat rather than a discussion, sermō (see talk).

Examples

  • advolā ad nōs eō animō ut nōs amēs, tē amārī sciās. cētera cōram agēmus.

    Hurry to us, ready to love us and sure that you are loved. We’ll discuss the rest in person.Cic. Att. 4.4.1

  • sīn es in viā, cum eris mē adsecūtus, cōram agēmus quae erunt agenda.

    But if you’re on the road, we’ll discuss what needs discussing in person, once you’ve caught up with me.Cic. Att. 3.5

  • Cōram id agere possumus.

    We can discuss that face to face.Traupman 97

  • Id cōram agere possumus.

    We can discuss that face to face.Traupman 105

  • Dē eō cōram disputāre possumus.

    We can discuss that one on one.Traupman 354

See also talk, debate, consider.
